Hi Olivia — thanks for the details and the usage export. We have two workable paths and a short third option (hybrid). High level: cost math below plus timeline and operational caveats.

Option 1 — Short-term top-up (fastest)
- Add a 3-month top-up bucket for +30% of committed units.
- Pricing: current per-token rate retained for committed units; incremental usage priced at +18% over committed rate (covers burst headroom & priority capacity).
- Timeline: can be active within 7 business days after PO.
- Pros/Cons: fastest to stand up; billing will show a separate top-up line and not co-term.

Option 2 — Annualize & co-term (predictable invoicing)
- Move to an annualized commit at the new expected run-rate and co-term all contracts to 31 Dec 2028.
- Pricing: blended rate across historical baseline and uplifted commit. We can offer a one-time blended discount on the incremental portion (12% off incremental price) in exchange for signed co-term.
- Timeline: 30–45 days (procurement + legal review + invoice alignment).
- Pros/Cons: clean billing and forecasting; requires negotiation on discount bands and legal signoff.

Option 3 — Hybrid staged annualize
- Immediate 3-month top-up at +10% incremental price, followed by a fast-track annualize within 60 days with a smaller incremental discount (10%).

Notes/requirements:
- All co-term offers require final approval from Revenue Ops and Finance for discount exceptions (anything >10% on incremental pricing needs exec sign-off).
- SLA and data residency terms remain unchanged in these options; any material change will extend legal review.

I attached a draft amendment and an SOW template showing the billing SKU breakdown.

If you like, I can model exact numbers against your usage file and send a clean quote + formal amendment for signature. Tell me which option feels closest and I’ll loop legal and finance.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
